messages:
Anu (devex): quick one — enterprise customer seeing `certificate signed by unknown authority` when calling redwood-py from inside corporate network. Happens with simple generate call. Any quick checklist?
Mike (eng-runtime): most likely corp MITM re-signing TLS. Quick wins: try curl with the corp CA, check system trust store. Example: `curl --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/corp_root.pem https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate`
Sarah (sdk): for python you can also pass `verify='/path/to/corp_root.pem'` to requests, or set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/corp_root.pem`. If they use certifi, `python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())"` to see the bundle path.
Lee (security): corp proxies often insert their own CA. The right fix is to add the corporate root to the OS trust store (Keychain on mac, certmgr on Windows, update-ca-trust/ca-certificates on linux) and mark it trusted for SSL.
Mike (eng-runtime): debug w/ openssl too: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts` will show the chain and issuer. If the chain shows a corp CA, that's the sign. Also SNI mismatch can produce similar errors.
Anu (devex): what about Node users? Customer reported `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE` errors from redwood-js.
Sarah (sdk): Node runtime accepts extra CAs via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` env var: `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/home/me/corp.pem`. Avoid `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` — that's insecure. We currently don't expose a per-client `ca` option in the hosted SDKs (file a doc + feature request).
Mike (eng-runtime): for curl and system tools on Debian/Ubuntu they may need to put the PEM into `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and run `update-ca-certificates`. On alpine, add to `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`.
Anu (devex): customer also asked about mTLS — they want to present client cert to our endpoint. Is that supported?
Lee (security): hosted API (public) doesn't accept custom client certificates for auth. We do support mutual TLS for Private/Dedicated deployments with network controls — ops needs to enable it and configure validation against a provided CA. I'll echo the nuance in a ticket.
Sarah (sdk): note for Private customers we should document how to supply client cert + key to the different SDKs. Example (curl): `curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://private-host/v1/generate` and for python requests: `requests.post(url, json=payload, cert=("/path/client.pem","/path/client.key"))`. For Node, many HTTP libs support `agent` with `key`/`cert` in tls options.
Mike (eng-runtime): also worth reminding them about proxy TLS termination — some corp proxies will terminate TLS then open new TLS to the destination which can break client certs unless the proxy is configured to forward the original cert info.
ci-bot: created issue #4321: "docs: corporate CA and mTLS guidance for SDKs" assigned to @sarah.
Anu (devex): thanks — can someone add a short troubleshooting checklist in docs (env vars, openssl command, where to install on linux/mac/windows) and a note on hosted vs private mTLS? I'll share with the customer once done. :thumbsup:
Sarah (sdk): on it, will open a docs PR and link the issue. Also will propose SDK option to accept `extra_ca`/`ca_bundle` so customers behind corporate MITM can pass a path or buffer.
Mike (eng-runtime): if you hit a mysterious cert error, paste the `openssl s_client` output here and we can point to the exact failing cert.
Anu (devex): perfect — closing for now, will re-open if they hit anything else. Thanks everyone :)
